title: In silico design of magnonic lasing in constricted waveguides
authors: Jean F. Oliveira da Silva, Rai M. Menezes, Milorad V. Milosevic
abstract: Analogue black-hole systems have been proposed in various physical platforms, including magnetic materials, offering rich physics and promising applications such as wave lasing. However, their practical realization and characterization remain largely unexplored. Here, we present an in silico study of magnonic black-hole phenomena in constricted ferromagnetic waveguides driven by spin-polarized currents. Using micromagnetic simulations with a two-dimensional Poisson solver to obtain realistic current-density profiles, we demonstrate the formation of a double-hole cavity bounded by analogue event horizons, enabling resonant spin-wave amplification. We characterize the resonances as a function of magnetic and geometric parameters and identify the corresponding spin-wave modes. We further show that gradual tapers enhance transmission by suppressing spin-wave reflections, while interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction can mimic the current-induced Doppler shift, substantially reducing the critical current density required for applications and, consequently, Joule heating. Finally, we demonstrate a spin-wave laser in which thermally excited spin waves undergo selective amplification and coherent emission at well-defined resonance frequencies. These results provide design principles for magnonic analogues of gravitational systems and point toward their potential for advanced spintronic applications.
summary: This paper presents an in silico study on achieving magnonic lasing in constricted magnetic waveguides by modeling analogue black-hole physics. Using advanced micromagnetic simulations, the authors show that incorporating interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction significantly reduces the operational current density. The work successfully demonstrates the coherent emission of spin waves, establishing design principles for advanced spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to design and understand magnonic lasing phenomena by modeling analogue black-hole physics in constricted ferromagnetic waveguides.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that the incorporation of interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (iDMI) significantly lowers the critical current density required for operation, and they successfully model spin-wave lasing from thermally excited magnons.
method: The research employs in silico micromagnetic simulations, utilizing a two-dimensional Poisson solver to obtain realistic current-density profiles for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
model_or_system: The physical system is a thin ferromagnetic waveguide with bow-tie constrictions, where magnetization dynamics are governed by the LLG equation modified to include Spin-Transfer-Torque (STT). The system exhibits magnonic black-hole analogues due to the Doppler shift induced by spin-polarized currents.
key_observables: Resonant spin-wave amplification, spin-wave lasing emission frequency, and the critical current density ($J_c$).
important_parameters: Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (iDMI) strength, applied current density ($J$), and geometric parameters of the constriction.
main_assumptions: The analysis moves beyond idealized step-like current distributions by using realistic current profiles from a Poisson solver, and it models lasing by including stochastic thermal fields.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the waveguide, the dependence of critical current on external fields, the spin-wave dispersion relations showing gap opening, and space-time diagrams confirming resonant amplification and lasing.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework (LLG equation, black-hole analogy) to simulating the basic resonance in constricted geometries, then refining the model by incorporating iDMI to reduce operating thresholds, and finally demonstrating coherent spin-wave lasing using thermal excitation.
why_interesting: The concept of analogue black holes and wave lasing in magnetic systems provides a rich platform for studying non-linear wave dynamics and energy extraction, which has parallels in open quantum systems and cavity QED concepts.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly models magnonic lasing in ferromagnetic waveguides using the LLG equation and discusses spin-wave emission, which aligns perfectly with the core theme of coupling spin dynamics (magnons) to coherent emission/lasing, a key aspect of spintronics.
